ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB=AC=AD=2$, $\angle BCD=120^\circ$, then what is the value of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, with A as the center and AB as the radius, draw $\odot A$, extend BA to intersect $\odot A$ at T, and connect DT, \\
$\because$ $AB=AC=AD$,\\
$\therefore$ point A is the center of the circumscribed circle of $\triangle BCD$,\\
$\because$ $\angle BCD+\angle T=180^\circ$, $\angle BCD=120^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle T=60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ BT is the diameter,\\
$\therefore$ $BT=2AB=4$, $\angle BDT=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DBT=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $DT=\frac{1}{2}BT=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $BD=\sqrt{BT^2-TD^2}=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$,\\

From the text, AB=AC=AD=2 and angle BCD=120°. Therefore B, C, D lie on the circle centered at A with radius 2, so A is the circumcenter of triangle BCD. The inscribed angle ∠BCD subtends arc BD; since ∠BCD=120°, the intercepted major arc BD has measure 240°, so the minor central angle ∠BAD is 120°. Then BD is the chord of a circle of radius 2 subtending central angle 120°, hence BD=2R sin(120°/2)=4 sin60°=2√3.
